newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Moslems prevent Serbs from home visits.
newsitem.headline: Moslems prevent Serbs from home visits.

text.p: U.N. officials accused Moslem authorities of organising a demonstration by Moslem women who blocked a visit by 10 Serb refugees to their homes in the west Bosnian town of Kljuc on Thursday.
Kris Janowski of the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said the incident was probably organised by the town's mayor who had promised cooperation.
"It's a purely farcical situation where the mayor is apologetic, telling us he can't control the crowd," Janowski told reporters.
"We've seen these things many times in the Bosnian Serb republic, now we see such visits being blocked in the (Moslem- Croat) federation."
The UNHCR has been charged in Bosnia's peace accord with developing a plan which would allow Bosnian refugees both outside and inside of the country to return to their homes.

Janowski said that Kljuc incident was worrying because it happened after a recent and successful Moslem visit to Serb-held areas in the vicinity, one of the few areas in the Serb part of the country to have allowed it.
